This PC

Run the controller here. Its data stays in a folder only your Windows account can open.

Another machine

Connect to a controller running on a server, a Pi, or another PC.

    No saved controllers yet.

    Connect to a new one

    https is required, except for addresses on a private network. A controller listening only on its own loopback can be reached through an SSH tunnel; connect to the tunnel's http://127.0.0.1 port.

    Set up a controller on a server

    Get a command to paste on a Linux server that installs the controller there, plus the steps to reach it from this PC. Nothing is sent from here; this only writes the commands.

    “Install it for me” logs in with the SSH key you already use (this app never sees a password), installs the controller, keeps the tunnel open for you and connects. It needs ssh user@host to work from this PC without a password prompt, and root or a user that can run sudo without one.

    Is this your server?

    This is the first time this app has connected to it. Check that the fingerprint is the server's own: your provider's console often shows it, or run ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key.pub on the server.
